title: Redesign filter Auto-Refresh to be incremental (scan only newly appended lines after initial index build)

summary.problem: When filter Auto-refresh is enabled, UI freezes because the filter matching behaves like a full-file rescan on each refresh instead of matching only newly appended lines.
summary.goal: Implement an incremental matching pipeline for filter Auto-refresh: build a scan index once (manual scan or first auto-refresh) and then scan ONLY newly appended lines on subsequent auto-refresh cycles. Reuse compiled filter across refreshes. Reset index + recompile only when filter changes.

assumptions: Log files are append-only during the session (no truncation/rotation handling required for this task).
Hyperscan is supported and used when pattern is compatible; fallback engine is used otherwise.
There is an existing indexing mechanism for file lines and an existing search/filter pipeline for manual filtering.
Auto-refresh button refers to auto-updating filter results, not the main file follow mode (but it should integrate with live appends).
scope: Filter/search results auto-refresh behavior (incremental scanning after initial scan).
Manual filtering behavior must create/persist scan state (index + compiled filter) used by auto-refresh.
Compiled filter reuse across refresh cycles; rebuild only on filter change.
UI update should append new matches only; must not clear/rebuild full model each refresh.
Threading: ensure background scanning does not block UI; coalesce refresh triggers.
out_of_scope: Introducing new user-facing settings (RAM cache, etc.).
Refactoring unrelated rendering/highlighting code except where needed to avoid full refresh.
Changing file indexing strategy beyond what is required to support incremental scanning.
deliverables: Incremental scan state implementation (index + compiled filter + last scanned position).
Modified manual filter execution to populate scan state.
Modified auto-refresh behavior to scan only new lines after initial scan.
Model/UI update that appends new results without full reset.
Unit/integration tests for incremental scan behavior.
Lightweight instrumentation/logging to validate scan ranges during development (can be compiled out or behind debug flag).
acceptance_criteria: If user enables filter Auto-refresh without ever running manual filtering, the first auto-refresh performs a full scan (builds index) and subsequent refreshes scan only appended lines.
If user runs manual filtering first, enabling filter Auto-refresh MUST NOT trigger a full rescan; it must resume from the saved index and scan only appended lines.

If filter expression or filter options change (case sensitivity, regex mode, predefined filter selection, etc.), the compiled filter is rebuilt and the file scan index is reset; next scan is a full scan for the new filter.
While auto-refresh is enabled and file is being appended to, the UI remains responsive: background scanning + incremental model updates only. No full-model reset per refresh.
No duplicate matches are inserted into results; matches found before remain, and only new matches from appended lines are appended.
Works with Hyperscan engine and fallback regex engine with identical incremental behavior.

implementation_plan.title: Discovery: map current code paths for manual filter and filter auto-refresh
actions: Use ripgrep to locate UI action/slot for the filter Auto-refresh button and how it triggers refresh.
Locate manual filter execution path (the code that performs the initial search/filter scan).
Locate the model/view representing filtered matches and confirm whether refresh currently clears and repopulates.
Locate file-follow / file-change notification path that results in refresh triggers when data is appended.
Identify the abstraction that executes matching (Hyperscan vs fallback) and where compiled patterns are stored (if at all).
expected_output: A short note (in PR description or a dev markdown file) describing the call chain for manual filtering and for auto-refresh refresh cycles.

implementation_plan.title: Define persistent incremental scan state (index + compiled filter)
actions: Introduce a new internal struct/class (example name: IncrementalFilterScanState) owned by the filter/search controller (per view/tab).
State must include: filter key (expression + options), compiled engine handle, last scanned position, and a monotonically increasing generation id.
Choose a robust last scanned position representation: prefer lastScannedLine (line index) if line indexing is already available, plus lastScannedByteOffset for cheap file-growth checks.
Ensure state is cleared when opening a new file, closing the view, or clearing the filter.
expected_output: New state type added and wired into the filter controller with clear ownership and lifecycle.

implementation_plan.title: Implement filter keying + compiled filter caching (recompile only on change)
actions: Create a stable 'filter key' computed from filter text + all relevant options that affect matching.

On manual apply or auto-refresh trigger: if filter key differs from cached state, cancel any running scan, reset scan index, clear match results, compile new pattern, and mark fullScanCompleted=false.
If filter key is unchanged and compiledValid=true, reuse compiled pattern; do NOT recompile on every refresh.
expected_output: Compiled pattern is created once per filter change and reused across refreshes.

implementation_plan.title: Full scan implementation that builds the initial scan index
actions: Refactor current manual filtering code so the 'full scan' logic is callable from both manual apply and first auto-refresh.
After full scan completes successfully, set scan state: lastScannedLine=currentLastLine, lastScannedByteOffset=currentFileSize, fullScanCompleted=true.
Ensure results model is populated exactly once during full scan (existing behavior), but do not rebuild again unless filter changes.
expected_output: A single shared code path for initial full scan used by manual apply and first auto-refresh.

implementation_plan.title: Incremental scan implementation (scan ONLY newly appended lines)
actions: On each auto-refresh cycle (or file appended event), compute the new scan range using scan state: startLine = lastScannedLine + 1; endLine = currentLastLine (or equivalent).
If startLine > endLine, there is nothing new to scan; return quickly.
Read only the text for [startLine..endLine] using existing file indexing/chunk APIs (avoid reading entire file).
Run the compiled matcher on just that new range and collect matches mapped to absolute line numbers.
Append newly found match line numbers (or match objects) to the results model without resetting existing items.
Update scan state lastScannedLine=endLine and lastScannedByteOffset=currentFileSize.
notes: Prefer reusing existing search code by adding an overload that accepts a line range or byte range.
If existing code returns global offsets, add a base offset/line so results can be mapped correctly when scanning a partial segment.
expected_output: Incremental scan executes proportional to newly appended data only.

implementation_plan.title: Auto-refresh behavior rules (manual-first vs auto-first)
actions: When auto-refresh is enabled:
- If scanState.fullScanCompleted is false (no index yet), run full scan once to build index, then switch to incremental mode for subsequent refreshes.
- If scanState.fullScanCompleted is true (manual scan already ran), DO NOT full scan; run incremental scan from lastScannedLine+1.
When auto-refresh is disabled, do not run incremental scans; keep scan state intact so re-enabling does not force a full scan.
expected_output: Enabling auto-refresh after manual scan does not rescan whole file.

implementation_plan.title: Threading + coalescing: keep UI responsive
actions: Ensure both full scan and incremental scan run on a worker thread (existing search thread/QtConcurrent/task system).
Add a generationId to scan state. Increment it on filter change or file open. Each running job captures generationId; discard its result if generationId changed before completion.

Coalesce refresh triggers: if a scan is running and new data arrives, set a 'pendingRefresh' flag and run another incremental scan immediately after completion (starting from updated lastScannedLine).
Never block UI thread waiting for scan completion.
expected_output: No UI freezes during auto-refresh; scan work happens off the UI thread and updates are lightweight.

implementation_plan.title: Results model update: append only (no full reset per refresh)
actions: Modify results model update API to support incremental insertion (beginInsertRows/endInsertRows) with just the delta matches.
Avoid calling modelReset / full clear on each refresh. Only clear when filter key changes or file changes.
Ensure match count label updates without forcing a full view repaint.
expected_output: Filter results grow smoothly with appended matches; no flicker or full list rebuild.

implementation_plan.title: Instrumentation for validation (dev-only)
actions: Add debug logs (behind a debug flag or compile-time macro) that print: filterKeyHash, full vs incremental scan, startLine/endLine, bytesRead, matchesFound, timeTaken.
Use these logs to confirm incremental scans never start from line 0 unless fullScanCompleted=false or filter changed.
expected_output: Clear evidence in logs that scanning is incremental after initial scan.

implementation_plan.title: Tests: unit + integration for incremental scanning
actions: Add a unit test for filter key change: ensure state resets + recompiles + full scan is triggered.
Add integration test with a temp file: write initial content, enable auto-refresh (expect full scan once), append lines, trigger refresh, ensure only new lines scanned and results appended.
Add integration test: manual filter first then enable auto-refresh; verify no full scan is performed when enabling auto-refresh (can assert using instrumentation hooks or counters).
expected_output: Automated coverage proving full scan occurs once and incremental scanning happens afterward.

implementation_plan.title: Performance sanity checks
actions: Create a local reproducible benchmark scenario: large file + active filter + continuous append.
Verify CPU usage per refresh scales with appended lines only, not total file size.
Confirm UI remains interactive during heavy appends.
expected_output: Before/after notes in PR description showing improved behavior.

implementation_plan.title: Documentation / UX notes
actions: Update any developer docs/comments describing auto-refresh behavior to reflect the new incremental design.
Ensure tooltips/labels still match: Auto-refresh updates results with newly appended matching lines.
expected_output: Behavior is understandable for maintainers and future contributors.

manual_smoke_tests: Open a log, set a filter, run manual match, then enable auto-refresh; append lines externally; confirm results append without UI freeze.
Open a log, set a filter, enable auto-refresh without manual scan; confirm first scan finds existing matches, then only new lines are scanned.
Change filter while auto-refresh is enabled; confirm full rescan occurs once and results reflect new filter.

guidance: Prefer minimal invasive changes: reuse existing search/indexing primitives; add incremental range scanning rather than rewriting the search engine.
Make incremental scanning the default path for auto-refresh after initial scan is completed.
Keep correctness under append-only assumption; do not add rotation logic in this task.

If mapping match offsets to line numbers is hard at the chunk level, consider a pragmatic line-by-line scan ONLY for the incremental range; but prefer existing optimized batch scan if already implemented.
definition_of_done: Auto-refresh never triggers a full-file scan after the initial full scan (unless filter changes).
Compiled pattern is not recompiled each refresh.
UI remains responsive during append + auto-refresh.
